prompt: Each fixed-size download chooses either a slow or a fast speed and keeps it throughout. Why can file size divided by the mean chosen speed underestimate average completion time?

options.text: All downloads must finish at the slowest speed.
options.explanation: The fast outcome still occurs and has its own shorter duration.

options.text: Arithmetic averages are undefined for positive speeds.
options.explanation: The average exists; it answers a different question.

options.text: The transfer spends equal time at each speed.
options.explanation: The premise samples a speed per transfer, not a time-varying schedule.

options.text: Duration depends non-linearly on speed, so slow transfers contribute disproportionately.
options.explanation: Compute duration in each outcome before averaging.

workedExample: The desired random quantity is completion time. Convert each possible speed into the corresponding time, then weight those times. Averaging speeds first changes the order of a non-linear transformation and expectation.
